Section 1: 
The UK Health Secretary, Jeremy Hunt, and actor Ralf Little, have engaged in a lengthy Twitter dispute over the state of mental healthcare in the National Health Service (NHS). The argument began two weeks ago when Hunt appeared on The Andrew Marr Show and stated that the NHS had overseen the most significant expansion of mental health provision in Europe. In response, Little called out the health secretary on social media, accusing him of deliberately misleading the public with false statistics.

Section 2: 
Little, famous for his role in the British sitcom The Royle Family, challenged Hunt in his tweet to take him to court over his claim if he could prove that it was wrong. Hunt, who had previously retracted a distrusted claim that there had been an increase of 30,000 mental health workers, fought back by posting data and daring Little to prove him wrong. The health secretary's response came after a week and he highlighted a series of statistics to support his claim.

Section 3: 
In return, Little fired back with over 40 tweets challenging Hunt's assertions, using data from Full Fact, an independent UK fact-checking non-profit. This lengthy reply from Little went viral and has been shared more than 15,000 times, further fuelling the online debate. However, instead of settling the matter, both parties continued to engage in this public dispute.

Section 4: 
On the following Monday, Hunt posted 26 tweets defending his position, although he lost the thread's chronological order which added an extra layer of confusion. He addressed Little directly, asking him to provide evidence for his bold claim of lying to the public. He also announced that 8,000 mental health nurses were currently in training and advertised a recent 25 percent rise in nurse training positions.

Section 5: 
Interestingly, Hunt cited a New York Times article from July to uphold his claim, an article that has since been corrected three times. This article was questioned by the former shadow minister for mental health, Luciana Berger, who challenged its credibility. As the Twitter row continued to escalate, it has enticed public attention and has increased scrutiny of the current state of mental health care services in the UK.
